card.intuition: A hardware or software component that distributes incoming network traffic across multiple servers to ensure no single server becomes overwhelmed.
card.analogy: A traffic cop at a busy intersection: instead of letting all cars go down one narrow street (Single Server), the cop directs them into 4 different open lanes (Server Cluster) to keep traffic moving smoothly.
when_to_use: Scaling applications to handle millions of users
Implementing 'High Availability' (if one server crashes, the LB routes around it)
gotchas: Session Persistence (Sticky Sessions): if a user's data is only on Server A, but the LB sends their next request to Server B, the app will 'forget' who they are unless you use a shared store.
L4 vs L7: Layer 4 is fast and only looks at IP/Port. Layer 7 can look at headers and cookies but is slower because it has to 'speak' HTTP.

steps.annotation: Incoming requests arrive at the load balancer from many clients.
The LB routes each request O(1) using the selected algorithm (e.g. round robin) and skips unhealthy servers.
Requests are dispatched across the replica pool so no single server is overwhelmed.
Health-check pings remove failed servers from the rotation automatically.
When traffic spikes, adding replicas scales the pool with zero downtime.

exercise.prompt: Identify the simplest load balancing algorithm that cycles through servers one by one.
